judgment.rationale: Both are PRIMARY ONE Performance Objectives (rank 0). The second SFI is 'count and read correctly from 1-9' (Number and Numeration / Whole Number), while the first is 'add two or three numbers from 0 to 9 with sum not greater than 18' (Basic Operations / Addition). Counting and reading whole numbers 1-9 is a foundational number-sense skill that supports the ability to add those same single-digit numbers; proficiency in identifying and reading numbers 0-9 plausibly supports success in adding them. This is a substantive pedagogical dependency, not mere token overlap, so a same-rank developmental direction from counting/reading toward addition is justified. The nominated lexical overlaps ('9','from','numbers','to') are corroborative but not by themselves decisive.

This does not substantiate a directional developmental dependency, so a symmetric relatesTo best fits the evidence.

judgment.rationale: Both are Primary Two Performance Objectives under the same Theme (Mensuration and Geometry) and Sub-Theme (Shapes). The first concerns indicating the 'square corner' of a 2-dimensional shape (Topic 2, Two dimensional shapes); the second concerns identifying and counting the edges of a cube and cuboid (Topic 1, Three dimensional shapes). They share substantive conceptual coherence around identifying geometric features (corners/edges) of shapes, but they sit in different topics (2D vs 3D) at the same grade rank (both PRIMARY TWO, rank gap 0) with no evidence that mastery of one supports success in the other. Same-rank developmental direction lacks substantive support, so relatesTo is the best-fit symmetric judgment. Token/trigram and page-proximity overlaps are largely boilerplate ('pupils should be able to') and do not establish dependency.
